newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares edge up in average turnover.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares edge up in average turnover.

text.p: Egyptian shares edged up on Wednesday in average trade marked for the second consecutive day by interest in a variety of sectors.
The Capital Market Authority all-share index rose 1.1 points to 387.87 in 57.48 million pounds ($16.93 million) volume.

"For the second day in a row even though there is average turnover it is well-spread," said broker Mohammad Abdullah of Intercapital. "It means trade is not all going in one sector and could mean the market is getting more depth and sophistication."
Brokers have said the pharmaceutical sector is gaining in terms of interest on traditional favourites cement and mills.
On Wednesday, Eipico/Egyptian International Pharmaceutical Industries was the most traded stock, closing 1.50 pounds higher at 212.5 in 10.85 million pounds turnover.
"Eipico is still cheap on a P/E basis," Abdullah said. "Some of the shares in the stock exchange which were attractive in the past are not seen to be doing well in the coming months.
"In mills, for example, it looks like supply might meet demand in the future," he said.
Commercial International Bank was the banking sector's most actively traded share, and it rose 3.91 pounds to close at 82.11 after shares worth more than 4.6 million pounds changed hands.
Abdullah said that it was likely to be a reaction to the share's recent decrease in prices.
Amriyah Cement was the cement sector heavyweight, closing up 0.21 at 89.01 in 4.12 million pounds trade.
The CMA listed Cairo Precision Industries as well-traded with 5.36 million pounds of trade changing hands.
But the share fell 6.10 pounds to 134.5.
Abdullah said investor interest had risen in the closed private company after news that the over-the-counter shares sold recently to raise capital would be listed on the exchange.
"This will add to the liquidity of the stock," he said.
The index for openly traded firms rose to 588.04 from 584.41 points on Tuesday and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms rose to 271.51 from 271.27.
Of the 85 shares traded, 37 rose, 28 declined and 20 remained unchanged.
